reader.notes: One grammar rule and one binder arm serve every organization, so the relative RESERVE clause is the sequential one by construction; integer-1 becomes FileModel.ReserveAreas and the connector's area count (DOC-A.1-164), with an implementation limit above 524,287 (COBOL2897). Several refusals at --std 85 still cite §2023 clause numbers in their text (COBOL1970, COBOL5506, COBOL2423), a message matter only.

refuter.evidence: r4pos-002 at --std 85: relative entries with the clause where §1985:VIII.2.3.3 SR1 lets it stand ('The clauses which follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order', cite.py OK): 'SELECT R1 RESERVE 2 AREA ASSIGN TO ...' (RESERVE before ASSIGN, singular AREA with 2), 'ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM RELATIVE KEY IS K2 FILE STATUS IS FS2 RESERVE 5 RELATIVE' (RESERVE between the ACCESS clause and a bare RELATIVE without ORGANIZATION IS), 'RESERVE 99 AREAS ORGANIZATION RELATIVE': compiled and ran, printing 'R1-REC' and 'R2-REC 00'. The reader's refusals (zero, signed, decimal, data-name, repeated, missing integer, RESERVE NO) stand. The grammar rule fileReserveClause and the binder arm are shared by every organization; the only edition sites are the diagnostic text and the closed clause list, which keep RESERVE once at 85. cite.py 'OK  §1985:VIII.2.3.4 GR5  (2.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5'.
